slides.title: GenericAgent GenericAgent https://github.com/lsdefine/GenericAgent - 8.6K stars https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.17091 GenericAgent
slides.text: GenericAgent GenericAgent https://github.com/lsdefine/GenericAgent - 8.6K stars https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.17091 GenericAgent is a minimal, self-evolving autonomous agent framework. Its core is just ~3K lines of code Through 9 atomic tools + a ~100-line Agent Loop, it grants any LLM system-level control over a local computer - covering browser, terminal, filesystem, keyboard/mouse input, screen vision, and mobile devices (Android Debug Bridge = DB) Its design philosophy: don't preload skills — evolve them Every time GenericAgent solves a new task, it automatically crystallizes the execution path into an skill for direct reuse later. The longer you use it, the more skills accumulate — forming a skill tree that belongs entirely to you, grown from 3K lines of seed code. DinTalClaw is a Chinese AI agent application - specifically a commercially authorized, packaged version of the GenericAgent framework built by A3 Laboratory (Advantage AI Agent Laboratory), a company based in Shenzhen, China - a joint research team co-founded by a Shenzhen company and a top Chinese university: Shenzhen Kuakua Jinglei Technology Co., Ltd.) - startup Fudan University Knowledge Factory Laboratory, Shanghai

slides.title: AI Google's Hope - POC Architecture - Continual
slides.text: AI Google's Hope - POC Architecture - Continual Learning Tackles a core LLM limitation - catastrophic forgetting when models are updated post-training Inspired by human brain memory systems, Hope uses a "Nested Learning" paradigm with Neural Learning Modules operating at different update frequencies, similar to how brain oscillations handle immediate processing versus long-term memory consolidation The architecture includes Self-Modifying Titans for immediate context and a Continuum Memory System with sequential modules updating at varying rates This multi-frequency approach creates redundancy that protects against knowledge loss Benchmarks show Hope outperforms standard Transformers on needle-in-haystack tasks, language modeling, and continual learning tests, while preserving scalability advantages over traditional attention-based models https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VTQR9n3aqNU Huashu Design - open-source clone of Claude Design Skill for Claude Code - performs comparably to Claude Design 63 skills, 27 commands, and 21 tools organized into 8 plugins https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Nmk1wxoi6ys https://github.com/alchaincyf/huashu-design

slides.title: AI Boris Cherny Six-step Claude Code System: 1.
slides.text: AI Boris Cherny Six-step Claude Code System: 1. Auto mode uses a classifier to automatically approve safe commands, letting you run multiple agents in parallel without babysitting them 2. Effort levels now include a new "extra high" default, which is more consistent than "max" since the model adaptively decides how much thinking a task needs 3. Focus mode hides intermediate steps so you only see final output, best kept on for builder agents and off for reviewer agents 4. A "fewer permission prompts" skill scans your history and whitelists common safe commands to reduce repetitive approvals 5. For long sessions, automatic recaps summarize agent progress so you can pick up where you left off 6. Finally, a short prompt style paired with a custom /go skill automates verification, code cleanup, and pull request submission in one chain https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VIbew55IpE4

slides.title: Claude Code - 15 Rules & Workflows 15
slides.text: Claude Code - 15 Rules & Workflows 15 rules and workflows used by the creator of Claude Code: 1.  Use the "--chrome" flag for front-end work so Claude can see and verify the UI 2.  Use "/branch" to fork a thread without polluting the main context 3.  Use "/resume [ID]" to jump back to a specific point in a conversation's history 4.  Use "remote-control" to pick up your terminal session on the Claude mobile app 5.  Use "teleport" to pull a session from mobile or the web back onto your local 6. Git Worktrees - run multiple Claude Code instances in parallel across different directories 7.  Use Opus for Everything - it is often faster and cheaper in the long run because it hits the correct solution sooner. 8.  Use automated loops to check PRs every 5 minutes and fix linting or test errors 9.  Use custom slash commands to combine skills and plugins into multi-step workflows 10. Use sub-agents for code simplification and app verification 11. Use the "/batch" command for massive tasks (100s of worktrees) 12. Focus on planning rather than coding 13. Maintain the CLAUDE.md File : Keep your project instructions concise, update them daily, delete and restart the file if it gets messy. 14. The "Grill Me" Process : Use a command to have Claude interview you about your plan to eliminate any ambiguity before implementation begins. 15. Use "/status-line" to track context window usage (tokens) and clear the context once it reaches 15-20% to maintain efficiency. http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qGAuqbbj1Ls

slides.title: Personal Agent OS Idea - Personal Agentic Operating
slides.text: Personal Agent OS Idea - Personal Agentic Operating System (Agent OS) A foundational layer of data and instructions that any AI tool (Claude Code, Cursor, etc.) can read, making your setup portable and reusable The framework has seven layers: Identity (your values and communication style), Context (org-specific knowledge), Skills (reusable workflow instructions), Memory (deliberate retention of decisions and relationships), Connections (integrations like email and Slack, starting read-only), Verification (periodic human audits), Automations (trusted background tasks) The key insight is compounding value. Once built, new agents inherit existing layers, making each addition faster https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ntvkDnk_5jA Google Gemini Deep Research & Deep Research Max Autonomously plan, execute web searches, and synthesize findings into comprehensive cited reports with native charts and visualizations, with MCP server support for querying private data alongside the public web. Deep Research runs ~80 searches using ~250k tokens (fast, ~$1.22/report) Deep Research Max doubles the depth to ~160 searches and up to 900k tokens for accuracy-critical tasks (~$4.80/report, up to 60 minutes). https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WXoBd5zgTxE Personal Agent OS — Identity, context, skills, memory, connections, verification, automations. Most marriages don't have all seven layers.

slides.title: China is Winning the AI Race http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=epzzALZ8oYo T
slides.text: China is Winning the AI Race http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=epzzALZ8oYo T he Chinese government subsidizes AI companies to "pick winners," allowing them to release high-quality models cheaply or for free 99% of business use cases (spreadsheets, coding, scheduling) don't need "frontier intelligence" from expensive models like GPT-4 or Claude. Consequently, businesses are turning to Chinese open-source models (like DeepSeek) because they are cheaper, secure, and customizable If the US economy is built on Chinese models, China will dictate AI standards and optimize models for their own hardware. This could force the US to eventually buy AI chips from China, creating a massive security risk. Also Chinese models may have Chinese bias and censorship 40% of the US stock market tied to seven tech companies heavily invested in AI, losing the AI race to China poses a direct threat to the American economy Meta & OpenAI - both turned to close-source model to fund its massive compute needs Anthropic has "zero" open-source strategy Nvidia is investing $26 Bln in open-source AI - because it profits when *anyone* uses their chips to run these models, making them the only US company with a truly aligned open-source business model Proposed Solutions to "Fix" American AI: Federal Support - Treating open-source AI as national infrastructure through federal grants, compute quotas, or tax credits Vertical Specialization -  Instead of competing with general frontier models, US startups should focus on highly efficient, vertical open-source models for industries like legal, biotech, and defense Encouraging AMD and Intel to follow Nvidia’s lead by funding open-source software to sell more hardware We're losing the AI race to a country we sold the chips to.

slides.title: From Transformers to Recurrent Models From Transformer model
slides.text: From Transformers to Recurrent Models From Transformer model to a Recurrent Foundation Model (RFM) https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.17121 ; https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BWRHhAnFMvQ Current Transformer models use a fixed number of layers (e.g., 96). Simple and complex tasks both receive the same amount of computation; Transformers are purely feed-forward, which limits their ability to track dynamic states and handle complex sequential dependencies; To "think" harder, current models must output text (Chain of Thought), which is slow and limited by context windows The Proposed Solution: Continuous Flow Dynamics Moving from discrete "Euler steps" (layer-by-layer) to a continuous vector field using Ordinary Differential Equations (ODEs) Instead of 96 fixed layers, the model uses a single recurrent block. A token stays in this "computational room" until it reaches a logical solution (an attractor) on a manifold Simple tasks exit the block quickly , while complex problems can iterate hundreds of times through the same parameters This architecture uses a single set of weights iterated over time, rather than unique weights for every layer The "Order One" Memory Miracle - by applying the Adjoint Sensitivity Method (a technique from 1960s physics used in aerodynamics and rocket science), the model can achieve significant efficiency Zero Memory Bloat - don't need saving every intermediate state in VRAM. The Adjoint method runs the "physics" of the network in reverse Constant Training Cost - Training for 10 steps or 10K reasoning steps requires the same amount of memory Transformers to Recurrent - After eight years, the field has rediscovered a startling fact: thinking takes time.

slides.title: AI Interview Question Question: How do you validate
slides.text: AI Interview Question Question: How do you validate AI output before shipping? Same way you validate a toddler's homework — carefully, and with low expectations. Response: I validate in layers, not as a single step: 1. Schema/format checks - Enforce expected structure (valid JSON, required fields, correct types) before anything downstream consumes the output. 2. Rule-based filters - Use regex or heuristics to catch forbidden content, PII leaks, or hallucinated patterns. 3. Golden dataset tests - Maintain curated input/output pairs that run as CI gates. A quality drop below threshold blocks the release automatically. 4. LLM-as-judge - Use a second model to score subjective quality (coherence, relevance, tone) where rule-based checks fall short. 5. Human review - Route high-stakes or low-confidence outputs to a human before shipping. 6. Production monitoring - After launch, track real traces for quality drift and error rate spikes. The key principle: treat evals like software tests. Hook them into CI/CD so validation is automatic, not manual. And apply the same standards at runtime as guardrails, so bad output never reaches the user rather than just being measured after the fact. For tooling, I'd mention Pydantic for structured output enforcement, Promptfoo or Braintrust for eval frameworks, and custom LLM-as-judge prompts using a model like Claude or GPT-4o.

slides.title: Dan Kennedy Book Dan Kennedy book "The Business
slides.text: Dan Kennedy Book Dan Kennedy book "The Business Owner's Emergency Survival Guide for the AI Revolution" Dan Kennedy's new book warns business owners that AI is dangerous because it pushes everyone toward sameness. AI studies what competitors do and recommends you copy them, which destroys what makes your business special. When everyone looks alike, customers only choose by price and location, killing profits. Kennedy shows how resumes, college essays, and marketing all sound identical now because AI wrote them. Even lawyers face new rules limiting their fees when using AI. The danger is worst for newer business owners who trust AI's advice and lose their unique voice. His solution: keep doing the basics well, protect what makes you different, and use AI carefully. The book is on Amazon - https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0GWYDTL8P When AI writes everyone's pitch, sounding like yourself becomes the moat. - Dan Kennedy

slides.title: About Job Search in the US Do not
slides.text: About Job Search in the US Do not use Monster.com or Dice.com . They used to be good for finding jobs, but now they are NOT effective, and can even be dangerous. Dice has become heavily populated by Indian-run offshore staffing firms. They scrape resumes and personal data, insisting on getting direct phone number, social security number, or copy of a photo ID All jobs are low-paying jobs. Many jobs are fake - used purely for lead generation. There is also associated identity-theft risk. Monster followed a different trajectory but ended up in a similar place. It's still large, but cluttered with stale or low-quality listings. It's widely scraped, and often yields spammy or irrelevant contact rather than focused outreach from serious employers. So, do NOT post your resume on Dice or Monster. Use these methods instead: LinkedIn - https://www.linkedin.com Hacker News (Who is hiring? threads) - - https://news.ycombinator.com/jobs Indeed - https://www.indeed.com company-specific career pages company-specific talent communities your own networking, referrals. Be skeptical of inbound calls or emails. Especially from offshore companies, not known, or when details are vague or mismatched.
